title: Barracuda reports Sneaky 2FA phishing campaign aimed at stealing session cookies
date_note: SecurityBrief's article of 26 November gives no earlier day for Barracuda's report.
sector: Financial services, insurance and services organisations (targets)
geo_basis: Barracuda headquarters; the researcher, not a victim
summary: Barracuda says it identified a Sneaky 2FA phishing campaign aimed at financial services, insurance and services organisations, designed to steal authenticated session cookies after users complete multifactor authentication. According to Barracuda, the lures were mailbox alerts sent through Google's relay service, smtp-relay.gmail.com, with a 'Verify access' challenge before a fake sign-in page where the attacker relays the Microsoft sign-in.
plain: Barracuda says a phishing campaign uses fake mailbox alerts and a relayed Microsoft sign-in to steal session cookies, which can let attackers in without repeating multifactor authentication.
exec: Barracuda says the campaign targets financial services, insurance and services organisations and aims to bypass multifactor authentication by stealing session cookies.
action: Barracuda advises phishing-resistant authentication such as passkeys or FIDO2 security keys, and revoking affected sessions and resetting passwords where session theft is suspected.

validation.note: One publisher: SecurityBrief (the Australia, Asia, UK and New Zealand sites carry the same article). Barracuda's own post was not found or read.

review.note: title, date, sectors, lure details and Barracuda's advice checked against SecurityBrief; single_source is right
